title: decentralized-staggered-decommitment-and-sla-hedging
author: Marcus Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet decommitment today is coarse-grained and can cause synchronized capacity drops that reverberate through tenant latency SLOs. This change introduces a decentralized, staggered decommitment controller plus an SLA hedging probe to reduce tail regressions during scale-downs and provide explicit signals for safe commit reduction. Design summary: 1) Decentralized Staggering: each pool controller computes a local decommit_schedule that uses a randomized offset and a per-pool "warmth multiplier" so adjacent pools decommit at staggered times rather than in lockstep. The schedule takes into account pool_warmth_index (EWMA of recent utilization and cold-start hit rate), commitment_slack (available burst credit ratio), and a configurable max_decommit_pct_per_window. 2) Adaptive Commitment Multiplier: we introduce a per-tenant multiplier that decays toward 1.0 if decommitting causes latency regressions. The multiplier is bumped based on recent 95th/99th delta measured by the SLA probe and bounded by tenant_min_multiplier/tenant_max_multiplier. 3) SLA Hedging Probe (Safety Sampler): a lightweight synthetic runner that periodically issues a small sample of production-shaped requests to candidate pools during dry-runs to estimate the decommitment confidence. The probe reports decommit_confidence (0..1), tail_delta_ms, and success_rate and is used to gate aggressive decommits. 4) Rollout & Feature Flags: default behavior is disabled; feature flag rollout begins with non-prod canaries, then gradual traffic rings with kill-switches. Backwards compatibility: controllers respect existing reservation and warm-pool configs; if the multiplier is unset we continue current behavior. Checklist: - add controller and metrics - unit tests for scheduling math - e2e dry-run harness using safety sampler - dashboards for decommit_confidence / pool_warmth_index - rollout feature-flag and canary automation - docs for tuning parameters and migration Notes on correctness: randomized offsets avoid correlated decommits but introduce small variance in capacity timing; the safety sampler ensures we detect regressions before they affect production. Telemetry and observability: new metrics exported under redwood.autoscaler.decommit.*: pool_warmth_index, decommit_schedule_offset, decommit_confidence, commitment_multiplier_{tenant}, probe_tail_delta_ms. Alerts: a new alert fires if any probe_tail_delta_ms > 200ms for three consecutive probe windows. Migration: config schema adds optional fields to fleetpolicy CRD (warmthMultiplier, decommitWindowPct, probeWindowMs) with safe defaults. Performance: implementation targets O(N) per-pool compute with a small CPU cost; we validated on canary that control-plane CPU increased by <7% at 10k pools. Rollout plan: canary in staging (week 1), controlled ring in regions us-west/us-east (week 2), global enable with monitoring gates (week 3).

review_comments: Priya Kapoor: Nice incremental design. Can you clarify how the probe load is accounted for in tenant billing? Marcus: Probe traffic is synthetic and charged to an internal observability pool; added note to docs and tag to all probe metrics.

Liam O'Connell: The randomized offset looks good but please ensure the RNG seed is not correlated across controllers. Marcus: Switched to controller-local seed derived from pool id and epoch; added unit test.
Diego Marquez: Can we expose a per-tenant 'safe_decommit' boolean from the probe to the API? Marcus: Added safe_decommit flag to the controller status object and included in metrics export.

Priya Kapoor: Is there an escape hatch for immediate rollback if decommits go wrong? Marcus: Yes - feature flag and a per-cluster abort API + realtime alert that triggers an automatic cancel. Added docs section.

bench: warning - probe harness adds small microbench noise but within acceptable limits
release_notes: Introduce a staggered, decentralized decommitment controller and an SLA hedging safety sampler. Provides safer scale-downs with new telemetry (pool_warmth_index, decommit_confidence) and rollout via feature flag. No breaking changes by default; opt-in via fleetpolicy fields.
